attributes.scope: INVESTIGATION lane (user-sanctioned; melee precedent): can a compiler variant reproduce pinned targets FROM OUR EXISTING SOURCE? (1) Catalogue the residual classes the 131 rules absorb (webfrank.json is the dataset; group by class: recolor-only, permutation, copy-form, combined, value-equality) and pick 6-10 REPRESENTATIVE pinned functions spanning them. (2) Inventory available compilers (build/compilers/ or the compilers pack — list every MWCC version present) and the option space (the project uses -O4,p variants; enumerate plausibly-relevant flags: scheduling, inlining levels, -opt options). (3) For each representative: compile its TU under each candidate variant/option set, fndiff the raw output vs target — ANY exact reproduction dissolves that rule family legitimately (record precisely which variant+flags). (4) Assess p6-style derivation feasibility: read tools/gdl/mwcc_p6/README.md (the 1.2.5s precedent that closed registry.c) and evaluate whether the dominant residual classes (live-zero remat, copy-form) look like an allocator-revision fingerprint — document the distributional evidence image-wide (same shape across N unrelated functions = the melee-style signature). NO webfrank edits, NO source edits, NO shipping a compiler swap — findings become records + a ranked recommendation; a compiler change is a USER decision. Everything in your worktree; scratch compiles under CV_scratch/ or build/ — never against main; parallel fleets please pick other TUs
